document: FTRO Phase-0 concept and snapshot identities
note: Task card section 11.3: living series carry a concept identity naming the continuing product line and a snapshot identity naming the immutable state actually consumed. Where the provider supplies no immutable snapshot PID, section 10 requires an FTRO identity composed from the concept identifier, retrieval time, byte checksum and recorded retrieval procedure.

artifacts.concept_note: Zenodo supplies BOTH a concept DOI (10.5281/zenodo.17107692, resolving to the latest version) and a version DOI (10.5281/zenodo.17107693, pinning this version's files immutably). The distinction is asserted by the provider in four independent fields: conceptdoi, conceptrecid, links.parent_doi (vs links.self_doi) and metadata.relations.version[0].parent.pid_value. CORRECTION: Phase 0 originally recorded this leg as requiring an FTRO-composed snapshot identity on the grounds that 'metadata.version is null'. That was wrong twice over -- the key is ABSENT rather than null, and a human-readable version string has no bearing on PID separability. Task card §10 composition applies only where the provider supplies no immutable snapshot PID; Zenodo supplies one, so §10 was never triggered here. See FTRO-DEF-024.
artifacts.metadata_snapshot_note: The version DOI pins the FILES immutably but not the record METADATA: revision 6 records six metadata edits between created 2025-09-12T16:09:41Z and updated 2025-09-12T16:22:22Z, none of which minted a new DOI. A metadata snapshot therefore needs revision + updated in addition to the version DOI.
artifacts.content_validation: Archive expanded and fully parsed by src/ftro/analyse_optical.py: 12 comparison directories, 252 .dat and 12 .yml members, 9,018,290 records read and 9,018,290/9,018,290 MJD tokens confirmed as exact 1e-6 d multiples. Content validation here is stronger than a shape check -- the whole archive is parsed.

artifacts.internal_version_note: This archive carries 7 wrapper FILENAMES but only 5 DISTINCT wrapper byte sequences: 20220228-r11040_V004_iGSFC_kall.wrp == 20220228-r11040_V004_iIVS_kall.wrp; 20220228-r11040_V005_iGSFC_kall.wrp == 20220228-r11040_V005_iIVS_kall.wrp. Institution designators present are GSFC, IVS, MPI, but only GSFC, MPI produced distinct wrapper bytes -- the others are redesignations of identical content. A chain consuming 'the R11040 vgosDB' must name the wrapper MEMBER it used, keyed by member SHA-256 rather than filename; the archive checksum alone does not pin that choice. The wrapper format's own InputWrapper keyword records wrapper-to-wrapper derivation.
artifacts.volatility_warning: This archive is a RE-RELEASE, not a frozen 2022 artifact. The internal anchor is the latest wrapper's RunTimeTag (see wrapper_records), which post-dates the session by years; the HTTP Last-Modified is secondary and dates mirror publication rather than the reprocessing act. The bytes may change again; the checksum pins THIS retrieval.

Every record declares retrieval_validation; the three git-hosted evidence artifacts are retrieved and content-validated rather than asserted resolvable on commit metadata; concept-level records carry not_applicable.

vgosDB retrieval time and procedure re-synced after a re-pin. A re-pin changes the recorded provenance of a snapshot identity, so it is a deliberate version change, not incidental churn -- which is why the content gate flags it.
